title: Thermal Wc built as T(eps^-1 - I)T can return 0 for extreme Coulomb scales; solve eps*Delta = (S chi S)T instead
symptom: Verified counterexample on the current OpenBLAS chain: S = 1e-200, chi = -1, T = 1e200 makes the intermediate product underflow and the routine returns Wc = 0 where the correct answer is about -1. The condition estimate is rcond = 1 and both backward-error residuals are zero, so every existing check passes.
root_cause: The direct form Wc = T(eps^-1 - I)T forms S chi S and then subtracts; when the Hermitian Coulomb roots differ by hundreds of orders of magnitude the intermediate underflows/overflows and the subtraction loses the entire answer. The bounded thermal screening core therefore uses the algebraically equivalent weak-response form: build eps = I - S chi S, solve eps*Delta = (S chi S)T with a general pivoted complex LU (no same-frequency Hermitian fill, no real projection, explicit column-major copies), then Wc = T*Delta (src/core/thermal_gw_screening.cpp).
minimal_fix: Keep the solve form eps*Delta = (S chi S)T -> Wc = T*Delta; reject ill-conditioned solves (rcond <= 64*N*machine_eps); add the scalar S=1e-200, chi=-1, T=1e200 regression and explicitly refuse the regime where intermediate information is lost, instead of returning a plausible-looking zero.
validation: Run the analytic 2x2 non-commuting S/T tests, the non-symmetric chi tests, the independent 1e-18 weak-response regression, and the extreme-scaling scalar case; require Wc ~ -1 (or a hard rejection) and that no case is silently zeroed.
avoid: Do not accept a passing run as proof of correctness — rcond = 1 with zero residuals does not detect this underflow — and do not restore a same-frequency Hermitian eigensolver fill or real-symmetry projection to make the solve cheaper.
